problem: Clarification in the proof for the Bellamn-Ford algorithm
proof_numbered:
0001 | While proving the correctness of the Bellman-Ford algorithm, we prove the following lemma:
0002 | 
0003 | > After k (k >= 0) iterations of relaxations, for any node
0004 | **u** that has at least one path from **s** (the start node) to **u** with at most **k** edges, the distance of from **s** to **u** is the smallest length of a path
0005 | from **s** to **u** that contains at most **k** edges.
0006 | 
0007 | We prove this lemma using mathematical induction as follows:
0008 | 
0009 |  1. Base case: After 0 iteration, all distance values are **infinity**,
0010 |     but for **s** the distance is **0**, which is correct!
0011 |  2. We assume the lemma is true for **k** iterations and now we have to prove it for **k+1** iterations!
0012 |  3. Before **k + 1**th iteration, dist[u] (which is the distance of **u**, from **s**) is the smallest length of a path from **s** to **u** containing at most **k** edges. Each path from **s** to **u** goes through one of the incoming edges **(v, u)**. Relaxing by **(v, u)** is comparing it with the smallest length of a path from **s** to **u** through **v** containing at most **k + 1** edges -- this proves it!
0013 | 
0014 | Now, I have doubt in the 3rd point. Let us say that in the **k+1**-th iteration the node **u** has got a new distance after some edge relaxations, now according to the above lemma, this distance must be the shortest of the distances of all the paths with at most **k+1** edges from **s** to **u**. Now, consider another node **w**, that has an edge to it, from **u**. Now, the length of the path form **s** to **w** via **v** will have at most **k+2** edges, but if this edge is relaxed to reduce the dist[w], then in **k+1**-th iteration itself, we will have included a path (to **w**) that has almost **k+2** edges right? Is it not a contradiction? Can it not happen? 
0015 | 
0016 | To be more precise I am unable to reason the fact that, the lemma holds true throughout the **k+1**-th iteration -- I am not convinced with the 3rd step of the proof.
0017 | 
0018 | If someone can explain to me the 3rd step or whole proof more clearly, it would be really helpful! If someone can share a proof that does not use mathematical induction will also be really helpful!
